---
title: "Search the playbook"
description: "Find a page, a section or a phrase anywhere in the playbook."
title-block-banner: true
toc: false
---

```{=html}
<form role="search" method="get" action="search.html" class="pb-search">
  <label for="pb-q"><strong>What are you looking for?</strong></label>
  <p class="pb-search-hint">A word or a phrase. Searching looks at every section heading and
  everything written under it.</p>
  <div class="pb-search-row">
    <input type="search" id="pb-q" name="q" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
    <button type="submit" class="pb-search-go">Search</button>
  </div>
</form>

<div id="pb-count" role="status" aria-live="polite" class="pb-search-count"></div>
<div id="pb-results"></div>

<noscript>
  <p><strong>Searching needs JavaScript, and it is turned off.</strong> Every page is in the
  sidebar on the left, the glossary ends with
  <a href="guidance/09-resources/r1-glossary.html#where-to-find-a-topic">a table of topics and
  where each is covered</a>, and <a href="guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/check-it-applies.html">check
  the playbook applies</a> has a table of thirteen kinds of work and where each one starts.</p>
</noscript>

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var MAX = 40, SNIP = 220;

  function param() {
    var m = /[?&]q=([^&]*)/.exec(window.location.search);
    return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1].replace(/\+/g, " ")) : "";
  }
  function esc(s) {
    return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, function (c) {
      return {"&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;"}[c];
    });
  }
  // What a reader types, and what this playbook calls it. Measured against the index on
  // 5 October 2026: "SRO", "PQ", "HoP", "AQAL", "SDC", "V&V", "tiering" and "signoff" each
  // returned nothing at all, because the playbook writes every one of them out in full. A search
  // that returns nothing teaches a reader the playbook does not cover the thing, rather than that
  // they used a different word for it. Written as strict JSON so that
  // `checks/search.py` can read it and fail the build if a phrase on the right
  // stops appearing in the playbook.
  //
  // Widened on 16 October 2026 against 147 queries written as a reader would type them rather
  // than as the playbook words them. Nineteen returned nothing: "artificial intelligence",
  // "ChatGPT", "generative AI" and "LLM" for the section on using AI tools; "mistake" and
  // "retraction" for a published figure that is wrong; "anonymisation" for statistical
  // disclosure control; "retire" for decommissioning; "urgent" and "rush" for work with very
  // limited time; "acronym", singular, where only the plural was here. Each entry below was
  // measured: the phrase on the right is in the index, and the entry reaches pages the typed
  // word does not.
  var ALSO = {
    "sro": ["Analysis Senior Responsible Officer"],
    "sros": ["Analysis Senior Responsible Officer"],
    "msro": ["Model Senior Responsible Officer"],
    "senior responsible owner": ["Analysis Senior Responsible Officer"],
    "pq": ["Parliamentary Question"],
    "pqs": ["Parliamentary Question"],
    "hop": ["Lead Official for Statistics", "Head of Profession for Statistics"],
    "aqal": ["Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead"],
    "qa": ["quality assurance"],
    "bca": ["Business Critical"],
    "atrs": ["Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard"],
    "rap": ["Reproducible Analytical Pipelines"],
    "sdc": ["statistical disclosure control"],
    "v&v": ["verification and validation"],
    "cop": ["Code of Practice for Statistics"],
    "ig": ["information governance"],
    "osr": ["Office for Statistics Regulation"],
    "uksa": ["UK Statistics Authority"],
    "wcag": ["accessibility"],
    "gdpr": ["personal data"],
    "cpd": ["training"],
    "llm": ["Using AI tools to do the analysis"],
    "llms": ["Using AI tools to do the analysis"],
    "genai": ["Using AI tools to do the analysis"],
    "tier": ["assurance level"],
    "tiers": ["assurance level"],
    "tiered": ["assurance level"],
    "tiering": ["assurance level"],
    "matrix": ["assurance level"],
    "grade": ["assurance level"],
    "grading": ["assurance level"],
    "banding": ["assurance level"],
    "dashboard": ["Score the impact"],
    "signoff": ["sign-off"],
    "sign off": ["sign-off"],
    "peer reviewer": ["peer review"],
    "assurer": ["critical friend"],
    "second opinion": ["critical friend"],
    "qa statement": ["quality assurance statement"],
    "acronym": ["Glossary"],
    "acronyms": ["Glossary"],
    "abbreviation": ["Glossary"],
    "abbreviations": ["Glossary"],
    "jargon": ["Glossary"],
    "terminology": ["Glossary"],
    "artificial intelligence": ["AI"],
    "generative ai": ["Using AI tools to do the analysis"],
    "chatgpt": ["Using AI tools to do the analysis"],
    "copilot": ["Using AI tools to do the analysis"],
    "chatbot": ["Using AI tools to do the analysis"],
    "mistake": ["turns out to be wrong"],
    "mistakes": ["turns out to be wrong"],
    "retraction": ["correction"],
    "withdraw": ["correction"],
    "anonymisation": ["statistical disclosure control"],
    "anonymised": ["statistical disclosure control"],
    "pseudonymisation": ["statistical disclosure control"],
    "small numbers": ["statistical disclosure control"],
    "retire": ["decommission"],
    "retired": ["decommission"],
    "switch off": ["decommission"],
    "urgent": ["very limited time"],
    "rush": ["very limited time"],
    "rushed": ["very limited time"],
    "representation": ["under-represented"],
    "data protection act": ["personal data"],
    "screen reader": ["accessibility"],
    "confidence interval": ["uncertainty"],
    "error bars": ["uncertainty"],
    "margin of error": ["uncertainty"],
    "customer": ["commissioner"],
    "requester": ["commissioner"],
    "stakeholder": ["commissioner"],
    "proforma": ["project record"],
    "paperwork": ["project record"],
    "audit trail": ["project record"],
    "scope creep": ["out of scope"],
    "handover": ["delivery and sign-off"],
    "publication": ["publish"],
    "open data": ["publish"],
    "model register": ["Business Critical"],
    "lessons learnt": ["lessons learned"],
    "post mortem": ["lessons learned"],
    "retrospective": ["lessons learned"],
    "upskilling": ["training"]
  };

  // The needle, as a regular expression that cannot be broken by what somebody types.
  //
  // Where it starts matters more than it looks. Matching anywhere inside a word made "IG" return
  // 104 pages, every one of them from des-IG-n, d-IG-ram or s-IG-nificant, and made "RAP" rank the
  // accessibility page first on the strength of pa-RAG-raphs. So a match has to begin at the start
  // of a word, and a query of three characters or fewer has to be the whole word, because a query
  // that short is nearly always an abbreviation and prefixing it matches half the dictionary.
  // Anything longer still matches a prefix, so "uncertain" finds uncertainty.
  function needle(q) {
    var esc = q.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
    if (!/^[a-z0-9]/i.test(q)) { return new RegExp(esc, "gi"); }
    var end = q.length <= 3 && /^[a-z0-9]+$/i.test(q) ? "\\b" : "";
    return new RegExp("\\b" + esc + end, "gi");
  }

  // Words too common to narrow anything. A query made only of these keeps them, because
  // "who to ask" is a page here and dropping every word of it would search for nothing.
  var STOP = {"a": 1, "an": 1, "and": 1, "are": 1, "as": 1, "at": 1, "be": 1, "by": 1,
              "do": 1, "does": 1, "for": 1, "from": 1, "how": 1, "i": 1, "if": 1, "in": 1,
              "is": 1, "it": 1, "me": 1, "my": 1, "of": 1, "on": 1, "or": 1, "that": 1,
              "the": 1, "this": 1, "to": 1, "what": 1, "when": 1, "where": 1, "which": 1,
              "who": 1, "with": 1, "you": 1, "your": 1};

  // needle() matches forwards, so "uncertain" finds uncertainty. This is the other direction,
  // which is the one a reader actually types: "critical friends", "assurance levels", "peer
  // reviewing". Only where four characters survive, so "ties" does not become "t".
  function stem(w) {
    var m = w.match(/^(.*?)(ies|ing|ed|es|s)$/i);
    return m && m[1].length >= 4 ? m[1] : w;
  }

  // The query as words rather than as one string. The search used to turn the whole query,
  // spaces and all, into a single expression, so it only ever found an exact phrase: "who
  // signs it off", "role of the analyst" and "commissioner responsibilities" each returned
  // nothing at all, although every word of them is on the site.
  function terms(q) {
    var raw = String(q).toLowerCase().split(/[^a-z0-9&]+/i).filter(function (w) {
      return w.length > 0;
    });
    var keep = raw.filter(function (w) { return !STOP[w]; });
    return (keep.length ? keep : raw).map(stem);
  }

  // The phrases to search for as well as what was typed.
  function expand(q) {
    var key = q.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ALSO, key) ? ALSO[key] : [];
  }

  // The same map, keyed by the stem of each single word in it, built once.
  //
  // expand() keys on the whole query, which is right for a phrase like "senior responsible
  // owner" and wrong for every query with an ordinary word beside the abbreviation. Measured on
  // 16 October 2026: "sro" found 39 pages and "sro responsibilities" found none, because every
  // word of a query has to be somewhere in the entry, and "SRO" is nowhere in this playbook. So
  // adding a word made the search worse. The same went for "pq deadline", "ig advice", "hop sign
  // off", "sdc protocol", "v&v activities", "tiering rules" and "signoff level 2", every one of
  // which returned nothing while the abbreviation alone returned plenty.
  //
  // Keyed by the stem because terms() stems what was typed before it gets here, so "anonymised"
  // arrives as "anonymis" and would otherwise miss an entry spelled out in full.
  var ALSO_STEM = {};
  Object.keys(ALSO).forEach(function (k) {
    // Phrases are matched on the whole query instead. An ampersand is kept here, because
    // terms() keeps it too, so "v&v activities" arrives as two words and the first is a key.
    if (k.indexOf(" ") >= 0) { return; }
    var s = stem(k);
    if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ALSO_STEM, s)) { ALSO_STEM[s] = []; }
    ALSO[k].forEach(function (alt) {
      if (ALSO_STEM[s].indexOf(alt) < 0) { ALSO_STEM[s].push(alt); }
    });
  });

  function expandTerm(w) {
    return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ALSO_STEM, w) ? ALSO_STEM[w] : [];
  }

  // Rank: the title first, then the heading, then the body. Somebody searching "uncertainty"
  // wants the section called uncertainty above the nine pages that mention the word.
  function score(entry, re) {
    var n = 0;
    re.lastIndex = 0; if (re.test(entry.title || "")) n += 100;
    re.lastIndex = 0; if (re.test(entry.section || "")) n += 40;
    re.lastIndex = 0;
    var body = (entry.text || "").match(re);
    return body ? n + Math.min(body.length, 10) : n;
  }

  // Every word of the query has to be somewhere in the entry, and the whole phrase sitting
  // together is worth more than the words scattered. Then anything the playbook calls it by
  // another name, at half weight, so a page carrying the reader's own word stays above one
  // reached only through the phrase this playbook uses.
  function total(entry, q) {
    var ts = terms(q), n = 0, all = ts.length > 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < ts.length; i++) {
      var s = score(entry, needle(ts[i]));
      if (s === 0) {
        // The playbook does not use this word anywhere. Try what it calls the thing instead,
        // at half weight, so the word counts as found and the rest of the query still applies.
        expandTerm(ts[i]).forEach(function (alt) {
          s += score(entry, needle(alt)) / 2;
        });
      }
      if (s === 0) { all = false; }
      n += s;
    }
    if (!all) { n = 0; }
    if (ts.length > 1) {
      var phrase = score(entry, needle(String(q).trim()));
      if (phrase > 0) { n += phrase * 2; }
    }
    expand(q).forEach(function (alt) {
      n += score(entry, needle(alt)) / 2;
    });
    return n;
  }

  // A line of the page with the match in it, so a reader can tell a real hit from a passing one.
  // Tries what was typed first, then anything the search also looked for, so a result reached
  // through a synonym still shows the words that were found rather than no line at all.
  function snippetFor(entry, q) {
    var tried = [String(q).trim()].concat(expand(q)).concat(terms(q));
    for (var i = 0; i < tried.length; i++) {
      var s = snippet(entry.text, needle(tried[i]));
      if (s) { return s; }
    }
    return "";
  }

  function snippet(text, re) {
    re.lastIndex = 0;
    var m = re.exec(text || "");
    if (!m) { return ""; }
    var from = Math.max(0, m.index - SNIP / 3);
    var cut = String(text).slice(from, from + SNIP).replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    re.lastIndex = 0;
    return (from > 0 ? "…" : "") + esc(cut).replace(re, function (hit) {
      return "<mark>" + hit + "</mark>";
    }) + "…";
  }

  function render(q, index) {
    var countEl = document.getElementById("pb-count");
    var listEl = document.getElementById("pb-results");
    if (!q) { countEl.textContent = ""; listEl.innerHTML = ""; return; }

    // A page's title is worth the same to every section of that page, so a page with fifteen
    // sections used to contribute fifteen results all scoring alike and push whole pages off
    // the end of the list: searching the site's own central term returned eleven slices of one
    // page and lost nine other pages entirely. The second and later sections of a page step
    // down, so the first hit on a page keeps its place and breadth survives the cap.
    var depth = {};
    var hits = index.map(function (e) { return {e: e, s: total(e, q)}; })
                    .filter(function (h) { return h.s > 0; })
                    .sort(function (a, b) { return b.s - a.s; })
                    .map(function (h) {
                      var page = String(h.e.href).split("#")[0];
                      depth[page] = (depth[page] || 0) + 1;
                      h.r = h.s / depth[page];
                      return h;
                    })
                    .sort(function (a, b) { return b.r - a.r; })
                    .slice(0, MAX);

    // Say when the list has been cut. A capped list that does not say so reads as the whole
    // answer, and somebody concludes the playbook never mentions a thing it mentions sixty times.
    var found = index.filter(function (e) { return total(e, q) > 0; }).length;
    // And say when the results came from a word other than the one that was typed. Somebody
    // who searched SRO and got sixty pages about the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer
    // should be told which name this playbook uses, not left to infer it from the results.
    var direct = index.filter(function (e) { return score(e, needle(q)) > 0; }).length;
    var alt = expand(q);
    var also = direct === 0 && alt.length
      ? " This playbook calls it “" + alt.join("” and “") + "”."
      : "";
    countEl.textContent = (found === 0
      ? "No results for “" + q + "”."
      : found <= MAX
        ? found + (found === 1 ? " result for “" : " results for “") + q + "”."
        : "The " + MAX + " closest of " + found + " results for “" + q
          + "”. Add a word to narrow it.") + also;

    if (hits.length === 0) {
      listEl.innerHTML = "<p>Try a shorter word, or open "
        + "<a href=\"guidance/09-resources/r1-glossary.html#where-to-find-a-topic\">the table of topics</a> "
        + "at the end of the glossary, or use the sidebar, which lists every page.</p>";
      return;
    }

    var out = ["<ol class=\"pb-hits\">"];
    hits.forEach(function (h) {
      var e = h.e;
      // The link text names the page and the heading, so it still says where it goes when it is
      // read on its own, out of the sentence around it.
      // Forty of the entries carry no section, and on four pages that gave two or more
      // results the same link text going to different places, which is the 2.4.9 failure
      // this page exists to avoid. Where there is no section but the link carries an anchor,
      // the anchor names the place instead.
      var label = e.section;
      if (!label) {
        var frag = String(e.href).split("#")[1] || "";
        if (frag) {
          label = frag.replace(/-/g, " ");
          label = label.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + label.slice(1);
        }
      }
      var where = label && label !== e.title
        ? esc(e.title) + ": " + esc(label) : esc(e.title);
      out.push("<li><a href=\"" + esc(e.href) + "\">" + where + "</a>");
      var crumbs = e.crumbs && e.crumbs.length ? e.crumbs.join(" › ") : "";
      if (crumbs) { out.push("<span class=\"pb-hit-crumbs\">" + esc(crumbs) + "</span>"); }
      var s = snippetFor(e, q);
      if (s) { out.push("<span class=\"pb-hit-text\">" + s + "</span>"); }
      out.push("</li>");
    });
    out.push("</ol>");
    listEl.innerHTML = out.join("");
  }

  var box = document.getElementById("pb-q");
  var q0 = param();
  if (box) { box.value = q0; }

  // Quarto writes a table's cells, and the two halves of a line break, into the index with
  // nothing between them: "a colleague within the teamLevel 2 someone with no hand in the
  // work" is one string. A match has to start at a word, and there is no word boundary inside
  // "teamLevel", so searching for that level could not find it, and any snippet landing on the
  // join read as gibberish. The gap goes back in where a word plainly ran into the next. A
  // capital that is not followed by a lower-case letter is left alone, so "GovS 010", "AQuA"
  // and "NHSBSA" are untouched.
  function unglue(s) {
    return String(s || "").replace(/([a-z.,;:)])([A-Z][a-z])/g, "$1 $2");
  }

  fetch("search.json").then(function (r) { return r.json(); }).then(function (index) {
    index.forEach(function (e) { e.text = unglue(e.text); });
    render(q0, index);
    var form = document.querySelector(".pb-search");
    // Search as you type, so the page answers without a round trip. The form still submits
    // without this, which is what keeps the result a real URL somebody can send to a colleague.
    var timer = null;
    box.addEventListener("input", function () {
      window.clearTimeout(timer);
      timer = window.setTimeout(function () {
        var q = box.value.trim();
        render(q, index);
        if (window.history && window.history.replaceState) {
          window.history.replaceState(null, "",
            q ? "search.html?q=" + encodeURIComponent(q) : "search.html");
        }
      }, 150);
    });
    form.addEventListener("submit", function (ev) {
      ev.preventDefault();
      render(box.value.trim(), index);
    });
  }).catch(function () {
    document.getElementById("pb-count").textContent =
      "The search index could not be loaded. Every page is in the sidebar on the left.";
  });
}());
</script>
```
